originalTitle: Australia news live: shark attack victim thanks donors after ‘incredibly difficult’ recovery; second fur seal dies of suspected bird flu
content: Alan Jones trial enters its fourth week The Alan Jones trial enters its fourth week today, with a series of witnesses expected to give evidence at Sydney’s Downing Centre local court before judge Glenn Walsh. Jones has pleaded not guilty to 20 charges of indecent assault and two counts of sexual touching against six complainants. The second alleged victim, known as complainant C, has finished giving evidence, and witnesses relevant to his nine allegations against the former broadcaster are next to appear. The court has heard Jones allegedly groomed C for a decade, resulting in the young man sending multiple explicit texts to the broadcaster who he alleges touched him without consent. After the younger man left his job as a driver for Jones, the two continued to text each other in a way “inconsistent” with C feeling uncomfortable after the alleged incidents, defence barrister Gabrielle Bashir SC suggested. Joyce steps in on One Nation’s migration target Barnaby Joyce says a fellow One Nation MP made a mistake on Sunday by suggesting the minor party’s migration numbers would not be much different to Labor’s, AAP reports. One Nation MP David Farley told the ABC on Sunday that the party’s migration policy would include an extra 100,000 people annually, to provide a necessary regional workforce, on top of the 130,000 it had already flagged. The overall number would be slightly higher than the forecast 225,000 people under Labor’s policy. The comments from Farley were soon corrected by party leader Pauline Hanson on social media, who said the policy remained to reduce net overseas migration to 130,000 people. Joyce said Farley had misspoken when he made the comments on migration numbers: Show me a political career where people haven’t made a mistake, and I’ll show you a person who’s not told the truth. I’m not going to throw anybody under a bus. When people are new in parliament, they can sometimes get things incorrect, and that’s what happens. God knows, I’ve done it enough. Joyce said One Nation’s policy remained at 130,000 people annually for net overseas migration. Victoria police race to identify man found with critical injuries The race is on to identify a young man found unconscious on a busy walking trail before he succumbs to his critical injuries, AAP reports. Emergency services were called to Moonee Ponds creek trail in Glenroy, about 14km north from Melbourne’s CBD, on Sunday afternoon after a passerby found the man moaning and unconscious. The man was treated by ambulance paramedics at the scene before being taken to hospital to be treated for critical injuries. Police said the man, who is believed to be aged in his early 20s, did not have any belongings or identity documents with him and nothing of note was found at the scene. He is described as Caucasian in appearance, about 175cm tall, with a slim build, hazel-coloured eyes with no facial hair and brown, shoulder-length curly hair. He was wearing a grey singlet top and ripped blue jorts, a style of baggy denim shorts, when he was found. He also has residue of dark red nail polish on some fingernails. At this stage, police do not believe the man was assaulted, but it is unclear how he became injured. Thousands of little penguins being vaccinated against H5 bird flu in Victoria – video Leah Stewart, the woman who was bitten by a shark at Sydney’s Coogee beach in June, issued an update on GoFundMe yesterday, thanking the community for its support during her recovery. Stewart wrote: After what has been an incredibly difficult few months, I’m so happy that I’ve progressed enough to build some independence, and I can finally see some light after all of this. I’m sorry we’ve been quiet on the GoFundMe recently, we’ve just been focused on my healing, and I’ve been actively trying to do everything in my power to get back to some sort of normal life. I still have a long way to go, but my recovery has been remarkable, and a huge part of that is because of the absolute army of love, support, prayers and encouragement surrounding my family and I from all over the world. That means more to me than I can say, and I truly believe it’s played a huge role in my recovery. Stewart said she feels like she’s been given “a second chance at life, and I’m not going to waste it”. As I get better, I know I’ll make something of this second chance and aim to give back even more in generosity, care, and love. I will forever be grateful for everything, and everyone, I’ve been given. You’ve inspired me to get better, not bitter. Watt says fur seal death from bird flu is ‘very serious’ but government prepared Murray Watt, the environment minister, said the first confirmed death of a fur seal was a “very serious development”. Watt spoke to ABC News Breakfast, saying the government had warned the H5 strain of bird flu was likely to spread and more mass mortality events were likely, but officials have also been preparing for that eventuality. He said: What we’ve been doing over the last couple of years is trying to build up larger populations of these mammals, so if we do have bird flu come, and it does kill some of them, we still have resilient populations for the future. I know it’s a distressing thing for Australians to hear but we need to be realistic. This is the sort of thing we have seen overseas. We’re very fortunate we’re the last continent to have the bird flu happen. But we’ve been preparing for this for some time. Watt said the government would continue to do “everything we can to ensure these beautiful creatures will be here for us for a long time to come”. The nightly parade of penguins on Phillip Island is a tourist favourite, but has recently taken on a more serious tone, AAP reports. As the little penguins toddled up the Victorian beach on Sunday night, many were corralled into pens to receive the first of two vaccinations against bird flu.
